name: hbm_su_static_bank6_clock7_1015

job.purpose: Candidate structural per-macro clocks: six distinct provider roots plus one boundary-register root. Previous bank r1 CTS insertion316.9ps/spread92.5ps/slew229.8ps, two SRAMs sharing clocknets. Actual one source per macro, no added data edge/retiming. Serial1111.111111ps unchanged. No route/replication qualification before physical slot/pins and TTsetup FFhold DRC0 nativeclock checks. Native CTS attempt1 rejected mixed raw-macro CTS roots; corrected explicit hybrid policy: six actual raw SRAM pin references plus one CTS root, no macro pin on a CTS source. Word-select flops remain on the existing register root. r3 (H-ELEM-B, coordinator 12:24): the r2 CTS measured raw macro clock slew 417.5 ps because all seven clock pins were clustered on the N face; each raw macro clock pin now sits over its own macro column on the face nearest its row (bottom row 0-2 on S, top row 3-5 on N, 20 um ranges at the macro column centres); register root clk + rst_n stay on N. No RTL change. r4 (H-SU 10-15 17:50): r3 gate WARN 0 fail but register-root TT insertion 234.5-275.5 ps (H-tree 6 buffer levels from an unconstrained N-face clk pin) > native launch 220: clk pin pinned at the N-face centre (140-160 um, beside clk_macro4) so the H-tree trunk starts over the sink centroid. No RTL change. r5 (H-SU 10-15 18:30): r4 route TT+130.87/FF+7.79 but DRC 12, all M4 shorts (clock leaf nets/a signal vs macro g_read[2]/[5] PG/OBS) at the macros' EAST edge x 344.6-347.0: the east channel (22 um) holds all 198 read_data/read_return pins, their output flops and the clock leaves. Outline 369.36 -> 390.96 um widens that channel to ~44 um (macros unmoved, W channel unchanged). No RTL change. Generator centres the macros (+10.8 um, both channels ~33 um); raw macro clock and clk pin ranges move +10.8 um with their columns. r6 (H-SU 10-15 19:20): r5 route TT+130.0/FF+5.31, DRC 6, all M4 shorts of clock-leaf nets at the EAST edge of the east-column SRAMs g_read[2]/[5], x 355.38-357.84 vs edge 357.91 = starting 2.2-2.5 um inside the edge, i.e. just past the 2.4 um macro-edge guard (the jog moved to the first free M5 track beyond the guard). Guard depth 2.4 -> 6.0 um (the depth that routed DRC 0 on the ds-coll lane_w / hrow5 SRAM edges). No RTL/outline/pin change. r7 (H-SU 10-15 20:10, coordinator: change structure): r4/r5 DRC 12/6 were ALL M4 shorts of the REGISTER-root clock leaf nets (clknet_*_clk) against the M4 PG/OBS of the EAST-column SRAMs g_read[2]/[5] at their east edge: one root fed both the W-face request/write registers and the E-face read-data/return registers, so its tree crossed the SRAM columns over M5 and dropped onto M4 at the east macro edge. Structure: the read-side output registers move to their own related root clk_rd (same serial clock, pinned at the E face centre; RTL pinned_bank RD_ROOT=1, every caller wires clk_rd to the bank clock); clk now only reaches the W-side request/write registers. No register-clock net needs to cross the macros. Guard back to the 2.4 um default; outline 390.96 kept. Bench: exact PASS + coherence/return/clock_halt/new rd_halt mutants FAIL.

structural_change: The read-side output registers (read_data/read_return, 198 sinks) move from the shared register root to their own related root clk_rd pinned at the E face (RTL pinned_bank RD_ROOT=1), so no register-clock net crosses the SRAM columns to the east macro edge where r4/r5's M4 shorts were.

pin_regs.reason: the RTL (ot_hbm_su_static_pinned_bank) already registers every input (a_pin/r_pin/wa_pin/wd_pin/w_pin) and every output (read_data, r_return) at the boundary; a kit-level flop stage would add a redundant read edge
